ev.q: CDC analyzed data from the 2022 National Immunization Survey–Teen for 16,043 adolescents
Recent trends in vaccination coverage were assessed by comparing vaccination coverage by age among the 2008 and 2009 birth cohorts
In 2022, 89.9% of adolescents aged 13–17 years had received ≥1 Tdap dose
Kaplan-Meier techniques were used to account for censoring of vaccination status at age ≥14 years.
In 2022, 89.9% of adolescents aged 13–17 years had received ≥1 Tdap dose
Among all adolescents aged 13–17 years, 2022 vaccination coverage levels did not differ from 2021 levels
By age 14 years, among adolescents born in 2008, coverage with ≥1 Tdap dose was 3–4 percentage points lower
Cross-sectional analysis was used to estimate vaccination coverage among adolescents aged 13–17 years.
Analyses of recent trends in routine vaccination coverage show declines in coverage by age 13 and 14 years among adolescents born in 2008.
NIS-Teen is a random-digit–dialed telephone survey

methods_quotes.q: Z-tests were used to compare differences in vaccination coverage by survey year, birth year, and among sociodemographic groups
Kaplan-Meier techniques were used to account for censoring of vaccination status at age ≥14 years.
analyses were conducted using SAS-callable SUDAAN (version 11; RTI International)
Sampling weights were adjusted for survey nonresponse, adolescent multiplicity (number of chances of selection)
Estimates with 95% CIs widths >20 might not be reliable.
Estimates with sample size <30 were suppressed and marked with NA.
